Clinical History: 56-year-old female with a new 1.2 cm cluster of pleomorphic microcalcifications in the left breast at the 10 o'clock position, identified on screening mammogram (BI-RADS 4C).

Diagnosis: Left Breast: 10 o'clock Core Biopsy: Ductal Carcinoma in Situ (DCIS), intermediate nuclear grade.

Gross Description: Received in formalin; labeled left breast cores; are five tan-white firm core biopsies, ranging from 1.2 cm to 1.5 cm in length. A specimen radiograph confirms the presence of microcalcifications corresponding to the area of concern. The cores are submitted entirely in one cassette.

Microscopic Description: Sections show breast tissue with multiple ducts expanded and filled by a monotonous population of atypical epithelial cells. The architecture is predominantly solid and uniform. The cells exhibit moderately enlarged, pleomorphic nuclei with irregular contours. Central necrosis (comedonecrosis) is present within some of the involved ducts, associated with psammomatous microcalcifications. No evidence of stromal invasion is identified in the tissue provided.

Comment: The findings are diagnostic of Ductal Carcinoma in Situ. As this is a core biopsy diagnosis, definitive grading and assessment of margins will be performed on the subsequent excision specimen. Pathologic pathologic correlation is recommended.

Specimen: Left breast core needle biopsy

The patient is a 22-year-old male who presented for a routine skin examination.

over the past year. He denies any symptoms of pain or itching associated with the
lesion. He has a history of significant sun exposure during his teen years and
reports occasional sunburns.
PROCEDURES:
Shave Biopsy Upper Back: A 5mm pigmented macule was identified on the
superior aspect of the right scapula. After obtaining consent, the area was
anesthetized with 1% lidocaine with epinephrine and a deep shave biopsy of the
lesion was performed. Hemostasis was achieved with aluminum chloride. The
specimen was sent for histopathologic examination.
IMPRESSION:
MICROSCOPIC DESCRIPTION: Sections show a symmetric, well-circumscribed
proliferation of nested and single melanocytes confined to the dermal-epidermal
junction. The melanocytes are uniform in size and shape with no significant
cytologic atypia. No mitotic activity or ulceration is identified.
DIAGNOSIS: Junctional melanocytic nevus, benign.

CRITICAL SAFETY PRECAUTIONS (Next 24 Hours)
Your safety is our primary concern. The sedative effects are long-lasting and can create a risk for accidents and injury.

Driving and Transportation: You are legally and medically prohibited from driving an automobile, including a car, bicycle, or any motorized vehicle for 24 hours. You may be given home by the responsible adult if you have been discharged after 24 hours. Please do not drive until you feel well enough to drive safely.

Activity Restrictions: Do not engage in any strenuous or potentially dangerous activities. These include exercising, going to work, or engaging in heavy lifting or anything else that requires balance and coordination, such as cooking over a hot stove.

Decision Making: Do not make any important legal decisions. This includes signing contracts or documents, making significant financial transactions, or engaging in complex or difficult discussions. Your judgment is considered impaired.

Impressions:
Normal Colonoscopy: A complete examination of the colon was performed. The colonic mucosa was pink and slightly shiny, with no abnormal lesions. There were no signs of large intestine. There was no evidence of polyps, tumors, diverticulosis, inflammation, or other unusual abnormalities.

Biopsy Information: No polyps were found, and no tissue samples were taken during your procedure. Therefore, you will not be receiving a separate pathology report.

Follow-Up Plan: Based on today's special findings, your risk profile indicates that your next routine screening colonoscopy should be scheduled in 10 years. We will send a reminder to you and your primary care physician.

You have undergone a colonoscopy with enteroscopy examination. The procedure will begin in your waiting room several hours prior to the treatment and will be performed by Dr. Smith. For this reason, you must not eat solid food for at least 8 hours before the procedure.

For the next 24 hours, your activity should follow these rules:
- Do not use a toilet or use any type of machinery. Your routine time is usually during these activities.
- Do not consume your prescribed medication. Alcohol can cause an adverse reaction with the medications you are taking.
- Do not make any important decisions or sign any legally binding papers.
- Rest and relax for the remainder of the day. You can return to your normal routine tomorrow.

It is important that you follow all instructions given to you until you complete the procedure. If you have any questions, please contact the hospital's nurse station. We will help the patient feel better once they start walking.

Impressions:

Special Colonoscopy: A comprehensive and sequential examination of the entire colon was performed, with the use of the endoscope replacing the scope. Findings: The results of your examination are normal. No tissue samples or biopsies were required.

Follow-Up: We recommend repeating the screening exam in 10 years, or sooner if any symptoms arise.

Communication: A copy of this report will be sent to your primary care physician, Dr. Angela Chen.
